_about: Showcase sources for this project's website (landing direction D), cut by .github/workflows/showcase.yml. Times are seconds in the NASA original. Licences and the reasons for every cut: docs/saas/landing-d-sources.md. A source is cut only when approved is true and sha256 is pinned; every source gets a vetting pack. cut_on_push controls whether a push spends an AI run on it.

black_holes.title: Shedding Light on Black Holes

crop.why: removes the persistent 'science @ NASA' insignia bug (top right, x 1650-1852, y 63-147 of 1920x1076) and the Event Horizon Telescope logo (top left on EHT frames); keeps the right-aligned image credits

segments.why: after the Science@NASA bumper and the science.nasa.gov screenshots (their crossfade's last ghost frame is 20.033 s); intro and myth 1

myth 3. Drops 84.2-138.6 (myth 2): an artwork credited Robin Dienel, Carnegie Institution for Science, licence unverified; narration naming and quoting Dr. Dan Evans (NASA Headquarters) over his photo card
outro. Drops 174.3-203.95 (myth 4): Stephen Hawking's photo and name card appear before its sentence ends. Ends before 'visit science.nasa.gov' and the NASA end card

black_holes.caption_detector_override_why: the myth 3 title card prints its spoken sentence for ~13 s and lands on one of subtitles.already_captioned's eight sample frames; it is a title, not running captions. The detector's real verdict is still logged to already_captioned_verdict.json

eye_on_neptune.title: Eye on Neptune

segments.why: 'It is an ice giant, a planet of monster storms, and a recluse rarely seen.' Starts after the Science@NASA bumper (crossfade end not yet measured)

'When you find this elusive planet ...' to '... deep beneath the clouds.' Drops 21-65: the dated opposition lines ('on the night of September 9', 'evenings in September') and two shots of people (stargazer silhouettes, a person at a computer)
Voyager 2's closest glimpse, the dark vortex, Hubble since. Drops 89-99: 'This opposition event also comes just after the 30th anniversary ...' (dated)

Neptune's seasons span decades. Drops 129-139: 'NASA scientists have learned ...' (says NASA). Ends before 'consider taking a look ... in September' (dated), the stargazer silhouettes, 'visit science.nasa.gov' and the NASA end card
